name: Max Junestrand
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Legora (legal AI platform, Stockholm/New York)
profile: Swedish founder who studied computer engineering at KTH and business at the Stockholm School of Economics in parallel while working as a programmer. In 2023 he joined Sigge Labor and August Erséus to build Leya (renamed Legora in 2025), a collaborative AI workspace for lawyers that went through YC W24, reached ~$100M ARR within about 18 months and was valued at ~$5.55B.
interesting_fact: Legora is used by 140,000+ legal professionals at 2,600+ firms and in-house teams across 80+ markets, despite its CEO having no legal background.
deep_cut_fact: He initially missed admission to SSE on a technicality - after retaking courses to raise his grades he forgot to upload the updated transcripts - and got in a year later as one of the final reserve candidates. Legora's internal motto LFG stands for 'Lean in. Fight for excellence. Grow together.'
notes: Highly visible on podcasts (YC, Pigment Perspectives, 20VC-style shows); comfortable with media. Legora press office is the published route.

name: Daniel Marshall
current_role: Co-founder and former Chief Scientist (2020-2022), Varda Space Industries; reportedly now an optical development engineer at Draper
profile: Daniel Marshall co-founded Varda Space Industries in late 2020 with Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov and served as its first Chief Scientist until 2022, when Head of Product Rodocea succeeded him. Aggregator profiles say he previously worked at Physical Optics Corporation on in-space fibre production and joined Draper as a senior optical development engineer in late 2022.
interesting_fact: Varda, which he co-founded, flies autonomous W-Series capsules that crystallise pharmaceuticals in microgravity and bring them back through hypersonic re-entry.
deep_cut_fact: Before Varda he reportedly led a $5M project at Physical Optics Corporation to manufacture ZBLAN optical fibre in space (unverified aggregator source).
notes: Common name; identity beyond Varda co-founder relies on an aggregator profile (theorg.com). No longer at Varda, so likely not wealthy via an active role; low priority. No published contacts found.

name: Sun Yuanwen
current_role: Founder and CEO, TOP TOY (MINISO Group's collectible/pop-toy brand)
profile: Sun Yuanwen, in his mid-30s, drew on operational experience at Uniqlo to launch TOP TOY for MINISO founder Ye Guofu in late 2020. The chain grew into one of China's largest collectible-toy retailers by focusing on blind boxes and figures licensed from top-tier IPs; Temasek invested in 2025 at ~$1.3B valuation and it has filed for a Hong Kong IPO. He holds ~3.9%.
interesting_fact: Unlike Pop Mart, TOP TOY chose licensed derivative products of major IPs over original characters after its first-year original-IP push failed; Sun says he doesn't see Pop Mart as a direct rival.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding TOP TOY he gained his retail-operations grounding at Uniqlo; TOP TOY's first store opened just as Pop Mart went public in December 2020.
notes: TOP TOY is a MINISO subsidiary; parent IR is the published corporate route. Interviews mainly in Chinese media (36Kr). Consumer/retail profile - weaker fit for energy/data-center podcast.

name: Miel Donkers
current_role: Founding Engineer / Principal Software Engineer, Dash0
profile: Dutch software engineer and Dash0 co-founder who works mainly on Dash0's backend systems and its integration with the OpenTelemetry and Prometheus ecosystems, after several years in observability. Dash0 (founded 2023) raised a $110M Series B at a $1B valuation in 2026.
interesting_fact: He built Dash0 features such as automatic OpenTelemetry schema migrations and exponential-histogram support, and contributes to various open-source projects.
deep_cut_fact: Away from work he rides a motorbike and goes mountain-biking and walking in the dunes.
notes: Engineer, low public profile; best approached via Dash0 or CEO Mirko Novakovic.
